prompt: Enter seats all. Type 1 3 saas — or all.

hardware.docker: docker build -t qpu . && docker run --rm -p 8787:8787 qpu
hardware.pi: Alpine aarch64: apk add nodejs npm && npm i -g @uuidna/qpu && qpu-boot
hardware.receipt: the boot passes iff qpu_prove holds inside the machine; a boot that cannot prove itself does not serve

seat.reference: the exact integer state-vector simulator; every reading above is computed there
seat.doctrine: a device that fills this seat and disagrees with the simulator is a driver bug, never a physics claim
seat.acronym: QPU here is a quantum processing unit. The VideoCore QPU (Quad Processing Unit, Broadcom; QPULib by Matthew Naylor, MIT, 2016) is prior use of the acronym — a classical 16-lane SIMD vector core — unrelated and credited.
seat.occupant: a classical SIMD accelerator computing the same exact amplitudes faster is an honest occupant; it does not make the seat quantum

priorArt.name: QPULib
priorArt.author: Matthew Naylor
priorArt.status: experimental, no longer under development — stated by its own README
priorArt.acronym: QPU there is Broadcom VideoCore Quad Processing Unit, a classical SIMD vector core, unrelated to this unit

modes.name: source language interpreter
modes.purpose: the kernel read at source level

modes.name: target language emulator
modes.purpose: the generated target program, for debugging

modes.name: physical QPUs
modes.purpose: the device itself, chosen by passing QPU=1 to make

priorArt.equivalence: AutoTest runs each test on both the interpreter and the emulator and checks they agree
priorArt.inherited: one kernel, several ways to run it, and a reference that decides which one is wrong
